scope: Proposition 3.9 (Saturation of a preserving split) of the manuscript “Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation” (preprints/Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-dimensional-wave-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 079 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 79299093c07ea305), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Retain the terminal family in Equation (3.13). After any finite sequence of inserted operators or splittings that preserves its extremal exponent, every dominant homogeneous terminal class again has the exponents p, d in Equation (3.12). Suppose a non-remainder level supplied by Lemma 3.8 at depth a ∈ (0, 1) preserves this exponent. Let b be its peeling threshold and z its total raw energy, summed over the intervals of that cut. Then b = κspa+o(1) , z = es−da+o(1) . (3.14) The summed post-synthesis energy has the same exponent as z. The conclusion holds for a further sublevel that preserves the output.
